wisdom.title: Morning Wisdom
wisdom.text:
🌅 0600 Morning Wisdom

The discipline of the wise is a fortress that protects the soul from the chaos of a fallen world.

📖 Scripture — Proverbs 19:15-29

Laziness casts one into a deep sleep, And an idle person will suffer hunger.
He who keeps the commandment keeps his soul, But he who is careless of his ways will die.
He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD, And He will pay back what he has given.
Chasten your son while there is hope, And do not set your heart on his destruction.
A man of great wrath will suffer punishment; For if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.
Listen to counsel and receive instruction, That you may be wise in your latter days.
There are many plans in a man’s heart, Nevertheless the LORD’s counsel—that will stand.
What is desired in a man is kindness, And a poor man is better than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life, And he who has it will abide in satisfaction; He will not be visited with evil.
A lazy man buries his hand in the bowl, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
Strike a scoffer, and the simple will become wary; Rebuke one who has understanding, and he will discern knowledge.
He who mistreats his father and chases away his mother Is a son who causes shame and brings reproach.
Cease listening to instruction, my son, And you will stray from the words of knowledge.
A disreputable witness scorns justice, And the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.
Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And beatings for the backs of fools.

⸻

🧭 Context Summary
Solomon concludes his instructional discourse by contrasting the fatal consequences of sloth with the life-giving power of divine wisdom. He warns against the seductive but destructive allure of criminal conspiracy, framing it as a self-annihilating trap that ignores the sovereignty of God. The passage culminates in a paternal appeal for the son to hold fast to parental and divine instruction, presenting wisdom as a protective guardian and a fountain of life.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a REAL MAN — Receives Correction

Brother, you know the weight of armor and the discipline of the drill. Yet, in the spiritual realm, the greatest danger to a man is not the enemy outside, but the pride inside that refuses to yield. The text describes a man who despises instruction as one who walks in the way of sin, heading inevitably toward death. This is a sobering reality for a husband and father. To refuse correction is to declare independence from the very Source of order and life. You must recognize that when your wife, your pastor, or your conscience rebukes you, you are not being attacked; you are being rescued from the pit of your own foolishness.

The fear of the LORD is not a trembling fear, but a reverent awe that submits to His authority. This reverence manifests in how you handle reproof. A true man does not double down when confronted with his sin. He does not argue, deflect, or storm out. He kneels. He listens. He repents. This is the mark of spiritual maturity. It requires a strength far greater than stubbornness to lower your head and say, "You are right, Father. I was wrong." By doing so, you acknowledge that the LORD is the ultimate Commander, and His word is the final standard of right and wrong.

Brother, guard your heart against the enticement of the world, which often whispers that you know best. The path of the wise is narrow and often difficult, but it leads to life. The path of the proud is wide and comfortable, but it leads to Sheol. Let the instruction of your father and the teaching of your mother be a garland of grace upon your head, reminding you of the covenant faithfulness that has brought you to this day. Do not let your pride steal the blessings of correction. Instead, embrace the discipline of the LORD as a father disciplines the son in whom he delights.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Receives Correction
• Review a recent conflict with your wife and identify where your pride prevented you from listening to her valid concern.
• Ask your pastor or a mature brother to hold you accountable to a specific area of spiritual weakness you have been avoiding.
• Read Proverbs 12:1 before breakfast each morning to prime your heart to value reproof over self-justification.
• When convicted by the Holy Spirit of a specific sin, confess it immediately to God and, if it involves another person, seek forgiveness without delay.

⸻

🙏 Prayer

Father, I come before You as Your servant, acknowledging that my own heart is deceitful and desperately sinful. I confess that I have often despised correction, preferring the comfort of my own pride to the hard truth of Your Word. Forgive me, Lord, for walking in the way of sin through my stubbornness. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, break my heart for what breaks Yours, and give me a spirit that is teachable and humble. Help me to fear You above the opinion of men, and to see Your correction as a gift of mercy rather than a burden of shame. Grant me the courage to submit to the authority You have placed in my home and in Your Church. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Submit your pride to the sharp hammer of correction and forge a life of obedience before the furnace of hunger consumes you.

first.title: First Watch — The Husband's Post
first.text:
🕖 0700 First Watch — The Husband's Post

Brother, today we examine the sacred duty of protection and the solemn weight of covenantal responsibility.

📖 Scripture — Deuteronomy 21

“If anyone is found slain, lying in the field in the land which the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance from the slain man to the surrounding cities.
And it shall be that the elders of the city nearest to the slain man will take a heifer which has not been worked and which has not pulled with a yoke.
The elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a valley with flowing water, which is neither plowed nor sown, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley.
Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come near, for the LORD your God has chosen them to minister to Him and to bless in the name of the LORD; by their word every controversy and every assault shall be settled.
And all the elders of that city nearest to the slain man shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
Then they shall answer and say, ‘Our hands have not shed this blood, nor have our eyes seen it.
Provide atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel, whom You have redeemed, and do not lay innocent blood to the charge of Your people Israel.’ And atonement shall be provided on their behalf for the blood.
So you shall put away the guilt of innocent blood from among you when you do what is right in the sight of the LORD.
“When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God delivers them into your hand, and you take them captive,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and desire her and would take her for your wife,
then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.
She shall put off the clothes of her captivity, remain in your house, and mourn her father and her mother a full month; after that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
And it shall be, if you have no delight in her, then you shall set her free, but you certainly shall not sell her for money; you shall not treat her brutally, because you have humbled her.
“If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and they have borne him children, both the loved and the unloved, and if the firstborn son is of her who is unloved,
then it shall be, on the day he bequeaths his possessions to his sons, that he must not bestow firstborn status on the son of the loved wife in preference to the son of the unloved, the true firstborn.
But he shall acknowledge the son of the unloved wife as the firstborn by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for he is the beginning of his strength; the right of the firstborn is his.
“If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and who, when they have chastened him, will not heed them,
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his city.
And they shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he will not obey our voice; he is a glutton and a drunkard.’
Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death with stones; so you shall put away the evil from among you, and all Israel shall hear and fear.
“If a man has committed a sin deserving of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,
his body shall not remain overnight on the tree, but you shall surely bury him that day, so that you do not defile the land which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance; for he who is hanged is accursed of God.

⸻

🗺️ Briefing Summary

This passage outlines the severe legal consequences for a son who persistently rejects parental authority and moral order. It establishes the primacy of the firstborn’s inheritance, ensuring that family lineage and provision are protected regardless of the father’s personal affections. The text underscores the community’s role in maintaining moral boundaries through the removal of unrepentant evil.

⸻

❤️ Reflection for Your Wife — H.A.P.P.Y. Husband — Protecting

Brother, as a Marine and a husband to Maria, you understand that protection is not merely a physical act but a spiritual posture. The passage in Deuteronomy 21 highlights the gravity of rebellion against established authority, reminding us that order is a gift from the LORD. Your role is to guard the moral and spiritual integrity of your household, ensuring that chaos does not take root in the hearts of those under your care.

We see that the firstborn receives a double portion, a tangible provision that secures his future. This mirrors your duty as the provider and protector. You must stand as a shield against the world’s chaos, just as the law demanded the removal of evil from the midst of the camp. Your strength is not for your own glory but for the stability of your family.

By upholding biblical authority, you teach your children that submission to God’s order is the path to life. Your wife Maria benefits from a home where the headship is exercised with both firmness and love. You protect her and your children by maintaining a clear, godly standard of conduct that reflects the LORD’s character.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Protecting

• Review your household rules and ensure they align with biblical authority, correcting any ambiguity.
• Speak directly to your children about the seriousness of rebellion and the comfort of God’s order.
• Stand firm in your role as protector, shielding your family from spiritual compromise.
• Provide materially and emotionally for your wife, ensuring she feels secure in your leadership.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom

Father, we thank You for the gift of authority and the call to protect Your people. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, grant us the courage to uphold Your standards and the wisdom to lead our families with grace and truth. Strengthen our hands to guard the faith and our hearts to love as Christ loved the church. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Defend the birthright of your household against the encroaching chaos of sin by establishing a spiritual boundary that honors the order of the Creator.

second.title: Second Watch — The Father's Charge
second.text:
🕚 1100 Second Watch — The Father's Charge

The Lord commands His people to uphold the sanctity of the household and the integrity of the community, reminding us that holiness is maintained through vigilant obedience.

📖 Scripture — Deuteronomy 22

“You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep going astray, and hide yourself from them; you shall certainly bring them back to your brother.
And if your brother is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it to your own house, and it shall remain with you until your brother seeks it; then you shall restore it to him.
You shall do the same with his donkey, and so shall you do with his garment; with any lost thing of your brother’s, which he has lost and you have found, you shall do likewise; you must not hide yourself.
“You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fall down along the road, and hide yourself from them; you shall surely help him lift them up again.
“A woman shall not wear anything that pertains to a man, nor shall a man put on a woman’s garment, for all who do so are an abomination to the LORD your God.
“If a bird’s nest happens to be before you along the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, with the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young;
you shall surely let the mother go, and take the young for yourself, that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days.
“When you build a new house, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, that you may not bring guilt of bloodshed on your household if anyone falls from it.
“You shall not sow your vineyard with different kinds of seed, lest the yield of the seed which you have sown and the fruit of your vineyard be defiled.
“You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
“You shall not wear a garment of different sorts, such as wool and linen mixed together.
“You shall make tassels on the four corners of the clothing with which you cover yourself.
“If any man takes a wife, and goes in to her, and detests her,
and charges her with shameful conduct, and brings a bad name on her, and says, ‘I took this woman, and when I came to her I found she was not a virgin,’
then the father and mother of the young woman shall take and bring out the evidence of the young woman’s virginity to the elders of the city at the gate.
And the young woman’s father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man as wife, and he detests her.
Now he has charged her with shameful conduct, saying, “I found your daughter was not a virgin,” and yet these are the evidences of my daughter’s virginity.’ And they shall spread the cloth before the elders of the city.
Then the elders of that city shall take that man and punish him;
and they shall fine him one hundred shekels of silver and give them to the father of the young woman, because he has brought a bad name on a virgin of Israel. And she shall be his wife; he cannot divorce her all his days.
“But if the thing is true, and evidences of virginity are not found for the young woman,
then they shall bring out the young woman to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death with stones, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel, to play the harlot in her father’s house. So you shall put away the evil from among you.
“If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die—the man that lay with the woman, and the woman; so you shall put away the evil from Israel.
“If a young woman who is a virgin is betrothed to a husband, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,
then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and you shall stone them to death with stones, the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he humbled his neighbor’s wife; so you shall put away the evil from among you.
“But if a man finds a betrothed young woman in the countryside, and the man forces her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
But you shall do nothing to the young woman; there is in the young woman no sin deserving of death, for just as when a man rises against his neighbor and kills him, even so is this matter.
For he found her in the countryside, and the betrothed young woman cried out, but there was no one to save her.
“If a man finds a young woman who is a virgin, who is not betrothed, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are found out,
then the man who lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife because he has humbled her; he shall not be permitted to divorce her all his days.
“A man shall not take his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s bed.

🗺️ Field Notes

This passage establishes the boundaries of holiness, showing that the Lord cares deeply about the integrity of the family unit and the protection of the vulnerable. It mandates active responsibility for one’s neighbor’s property and the severe punishment for sexual immorality, reflecting the gravity of sin in the covenant community. The laws regarding virginity and marriage underscore the seriousness of sexual purity and the consequences of violating that trust. As a military man, you recognize the need for clear rules of engagement to maintain order and safety; these laws serve a similar purpose in the spiritual life of Israel.

🸻

👨‍👧 Reflection for Your Children — F.U.L.F.I.L.L.E.D. Father — Disciplining

Brother, look at how seriously God takes the protection of the innocent and the sanctity of the marriage covenant. In your watch, you see how disorder leads to destruction, and in this text, we see that holiness requires decisive action against sin. You are called to be a man of integrity, protecting your family from the encroachments of the enemy.

For Gideon, who is nineteen, understand that your strength must be governed by wisdom and self-control. The law against mixing kinds reminds you that you must not compromise your distinct call to Christ by blending with the world’s values. Guard your heart and your purity, for your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.

For Boaz, fourteen years old, know that your father’s discipline is not arbitrary but rooted in love and truth. The severe penalties for sexual sin show that God protects the innocent and holds men accountable for their actions. Do not despise correction, but submit to it, knowing that it shapes you into a man after God’s own heart.

For Shiloh, five years old, learn early that your father’s house is a place of order and safety. The commands to care for lost animals and to build safety rails show that God provides for the weak and expects us to do the same. Your father’s discipline is a shield, keeping you from harm and guiding you toward godly womanhood and feminine flourishing.

🸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Disciplining

• Review your household’s boundaries regarding media and influences, ensuring you do not "yoke" yourself with worldly practices that compromise your witness.
• Establish clear, consistent consequences for disobedience in your sons, reflecting the seriousness of sin without losing your temper.
• Protect your wife’s honor and your children’s purity by actively monitoring and guiding their interactions with the culture.
• Pray for the grace to execute discipline with love, remembering that the goal is restoration and the glory of God.

🙏 Prayer from the Wardroom

Father, we thank You for the clear instructions You have given for the order of Your house. Forgive us for the times we have been negligent in guarding our homes and hearts. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, give me the courage to uphold Your standards and the wisdom to apply them with grace. Protect my sons from the snares of the enemy and guide them into the truth of Your Word. Make me a faithful commander in my home, reflecting Your justice and mercy. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Brother, when you spot the stray burden of another, do not let it wander into the shadows, but seize it and escort it home to its rightful master.

third.title: Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand
third.text:
🕒 1500 Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand

The boundaries of holiness define the peace of the community, requiring a man to guard his tongue and his heart against the defilement that separates us from God.

📖 Scripture — Deuteronomy 23

“He who is emasculated by crushing or mutilation shall not enter the assembly of the LORD.
“One of illegitimate birth shall not enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
“An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD forever,
because they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.
Nevertheless the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, but the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
You shall not seek their peace nor their prosperity all your days forever.
“You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were an alien in his land.
The children of the third generation born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD.
“When the army goes out against your enemies, then keep yourself from every wicked thing.
If there is any man among you who becomes unclean by some occurrence in the night, then he shall go outside the camp; he shall not come inside the camp.
But it shall be, when evening comes, that he shall wash with water; and when the sun sets, he may come into the camp.
“Also you shall have a place outside the camp, where you may go out;
and you shall have an implement among your equipment, and when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn and cover your refuse.
For the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and give your enemies over to you; therefore your camp shall be holy, that He may see no unclean thing among you, and turn away from you.
“You shall not give back to his master the slave who has escaped from his master to you.
He may dwell with you in your midst, in the place which he chooses within one of your gates, where it seems best to him; you shall not oppress him.
“There shall be no ritual harlot of the daughters of Israel, or a perverted one of the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the wages of a harlot or the price of a dog to the house of the LORD your God for any vowed offering, for both of these are an abomination to the LORD your God.
“You shall not charge interest to your brother—interest on money or food or anything that is lent out at interest.
To a foreigner you may charge interest, but to your brother you shall not charge interest, that the LORD your God may bless you in all to which you set your hand in the land which you are entering to possess.
“When you make a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it; for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and it would be sin to you.
But if you abstain from vowing, it shall not be sin to you.
That which has gone from your lips you shall keep and perform, for you voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God what you have promised with your mouth.
“When you come into your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes at your pleasure, but you shall not put any in your container.
When you come into your neighbor’s standing grain, you may pluck the heads with your hand, but you shall not use a sickle on your neighbor’s standing grain.

⸻

🛰️ Situation Report
The Lord establishes clear boundaries for His people to maintain the purity and unity of His assembly. As a citizen of God’s kingdom, you are called to uphold these standards, recognizing that holiness is not merely personal but communal. Your conduct directly impacts the witness and stability of the church you serve.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a R.E.S.O.L.U.T.E. Citizen — Obedient

Fredericksburg (local)
Brother, in the streets of Fredericksburg, the call to obedience is not abstract but lived in the daily discipline of keeping your word. When you promise to be home for dinner, to meet a debt, or to attend a church meeting, your "yes" must be as solid as the stone walls around us. Obedience is the faithful execution of what is commanded, and it begins with the integrity of your speech. You are a man of your word, brother, because you serve a God who is perfectly truthful. Your household looks to you to model this reliability, seeing in your actions that God’s commands are good and necessary for our flourishing.

Virginia (state)
In this state, we see the tension between the law and the grace that covers our failures, yet the standard remains high. The exclusion of certain conditions from the assembly points to the seriousness with which God treats the body of believers. As a father and a husband in Virginia, you understand that leadership requires a clean record and a pure heart. You cannot lead what you do not love, and you cannot love what you do not obey. The Lord demands that we do not despise our neighbors, even those who have wronged us, for we are called to a higher standard of conduct. Your obedience in the state is demonstrated by your respect for authority and your commitment to justice, reflecting the order of God’s creation.

United States (nation)
The nation is built on the foundation of covenants, and you, as a citizen, are bound by the oaths you have sworn. To break a vow is to undermine the very fabric of society. The Lord reminds us that we were strangers in Egypt, and thus we are to treat the alien with justice and kindness. This is the mark of a godly nation: one that upholds the sanctity of vows and cares for the vulnerable. As a Marine veteran and a father, you know that discipline is the bridge between chaos and order. Your obedience to God’s law is your contribution to the moral health of this country, standing as a beacon of truth in a world that often despises the very commands that preserve it.

⛏️ Personal Application — Obedient
• Review your recent promises and immediately fulfill any that are pending, regardless of the cost.
• Examine your speech for any hint of deceit or half-truths, and commit to absolute honesty in all dealings.
• Study the character of God’s faithfulness in Deuteronomy 23 and meditate on how His obedience to the Father models your own.
• Speak a clear, affirmative "yes" or "no" to your family regarding upcoming commitments, ensuring your word is reliable.

🙏 Prayer from the Bridge
Father, we thank You for the clear boundaries You have set for Your people. Forgive us for our slowness to obey and our tendency toslight  Your commands. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, grant us the grace to keep our vows and to speak truth in our hearts. Strengthen our hands to do what is right and our hearts to love our neighbors as ourselves. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Inspect the integrity of your lineage and the purity of your vow, for the assembly of the LORD admits no broken vessel or illegitimate heir.

🦅 This Day in American History — March 19
On March 19, 1918, President Woodrow Wilson signed the Standard Time Act, ordering the whole nation onto common time zones so that a people at war might labor in step. On the same day in 1687, the great French explorer Robert de La Salle, who had claimed the Mississippi for empire, was shot dead by his own mutinous men on the banks of the Trinity River in what is now Texas. An Obedient citizen weighs the two ends, for one nation ordered itself willingly for the common good while one company cast off all authority and destroyed itself, and he chooses gladly the yoke of lawful order under God.

peace.title: Evening Peace
peace.text:
🌙 2100 Evening Peace

The day’s labor yields to the quiet watch, where the soul finds its truest rest in the Lord.

📖 Scripture — Psalm 69:19-36

You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor; My adversaries are all before You.
Reproach has broken my heart, And I am full of heaviness; I looked for someone to take pity, but there was none; And for comforters, but I found none.
They also gave me gall for my food, And for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table become a snare before them, And their well-being a trap.
Let their eyes be darkened, so that they do not see; And make their loins shake continually.
Pour out Your indignation upon them, And let Your wrathful anger take hold of them.
Let their dwelling place be desolate; Let no one live in their tents.
For they persecute the ones You have struck, And talk of the grief of those You have wounded.
Add iniquity to their iniquity, And let them not come into Your righteousness.
Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, And not be written with the righteous.
But I am poor and sorrowful; Let Your salvation, O God, set me up on high.
I will praise the name of God with a song, And will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
This also shall please the LORD better than an ox or bull, Which has horns and hooves.
The humble shall see this and be glad; And you who seek God, your hearts shall live.
For the LORD hears the poor, And does not despise His prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise Him, The seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion And build the cities of Judah, That they may dwell there and possess it.
Also, the descendants of His servants shall inherit it, And those who love His name shall dwell in it.

⸻

🌾 Reflection for a Man at Home and in Community

As a HAPPY husband, you recognize that the Lord sees the hidden burdens of your household with perfect clarity. He knows the weight of the reproach you carry to protect your wife and children, and He does not despise the quiet sacrifices you make to keep the covenant pure. Your strength is not found in avoiding pain, but in bringing your weary spirit before Him, trusting that He hears the poor in spirit and will not turn away from those who seek His face in the sanctity of your home.

As a FULFILLED father, you understand that true comfort is not found in the world’s empty promises but in the steadfast love of the Creator. When your children face the harshness of a fallen world, you stand as a living testament to the truth that God saves Zion and builds up the cities of Judah. You teach them that their inheritance is secure not in earthly wealth, but in the name of the LORD, encouraging them to look to Him for deliverance and to find their deepest joy in the fear of the Lord.

As a RESOLUTE citizen, you stand firm against the encroaching darkness, knowing that the Lord’s indignation is real and His justice is sure. You do not shrink from the battle, nor do you rely on the shifting sand of human approval. Instead, you anchor your hope in the promise that the humble shall see it and be glad, finding your revival in the knowledge that God hears the cry of the afflicted. Let your life be a song of praise, magnifying Him who sets the lowly on high and blots out the guilt of those who trust in His mercy.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom

Father, I thank You for the peace of this evening watch and for the privilege of leading my household in Your truth. I confess that I often bear the weight of my duties with heaviness, yet I know You see my reproach and my shame. I cast all my anxieties upon You, for You care for me. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen my hands to provide, my heart to love, and my mind to discern Your will in every decision I make for my family and my community. Guard my tongue from bitterness and my eyes from compromise, that I may remain faithful to the covenant I have made before You. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, who intercedes for me always, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Cast the heavy gall of your silent grief into the divine forge to temper your spirit for the covenant watch.
